correctness.rationale: For p<q<r distinct primes, S=p+q+r lies strictly in (r,qr), and if S divides the squarefree number pqr then it equals pq or pr, since the remaining divisors are outside that interval. S=pr gives q=(p-1)r-p, incompatible with q<r for p>=3; hence p=2 and r=q+2 (twin prime). S=pq gives r=pq-p-q>q, which forces p>=3. Both converse branches divide pqr, and the branches are disjoint. The bounding inequality holds even p=2,q=3. I independently factor-enumerated all squarefree three-prime n<=60000 and obtained exactly the two branch types; finite enumeration is corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge exact classification of a canonical three-prime layer of the De Koninck-Luca beta(n)|n problem. Their full primary 2005 paper proves global counting bounds and uses large-prime estimates, not the complete p<q<r two-branch divisor interval. OEIS A158804 is an exact list without this exhaustive parameterization. Natural overlap includes old examples 30,70,105 and the beta function itself; novelty is the complete iff.
residual_risks: A short divisor-interval classification may be reproduced in unindexed contest/problem notes or an appendix not found by statement search.

value.rationale: A natural and non-arbitrary first nontrivial three-distinct-prime support classification for a literature-studied divisibility property, separating twin prime and shifted-product prime families with an exact divisor identity. This can be used to test density and infinitude issues without pretending to solve them.

scientific_limitations: Only squarefree three distinct primes and only structural parametrization; twin-prime and shifted-prime infinitude remain open.
